history.period: 19th century (idol received 1860; reconstruction 1871); sanctum reportedly rebuilt by Ahilyabai Holkar; an 1865 British gazetteer already noted its great but unproven antiquity
history.summary: The Gramdaivat (tutelary city deity) of Jalgaon city and the ancient temple of the district. Shri Sadguru Appa Maharaj established Shri Ram Mandir as a religious centre of Khandesh; at a young age he received a divine idol of Prabhu Ram from Shri Ramanand Swami of the Ramanuj community, Ayodhya, in 1860, and the temple was reconstructed in 1871 into its present appearance. The 1865 British gazetteer recorded that there is no proved record of how ancient the temple is; the Dharmayug magazine (1985) reported that the sanctum was re-constructed by Ahilyabai Holkar. The temple trust's managing board (Shri Ram Trust Vishvasta Mandal) maintains it; locals organise many cultural programmes at the temple.

name: Shri Ram Mandir, Rampeth (Gramdaivat of Jalgaon)
town_description: Jalgaon is the largest city of the Khandesh region and the headquarters of Jalgaon district in North Maharashtra, a major banana-producing and trading hub. It lies on the main Mumbai-Bhopal rail line and NH-53, about 400 km northeast of Mumbai. Rampeth is an old locality of the city where the Sansthan's temple stands.

travel.airport: Jalgaon Airport (~6 km from city centre; no scheduled services as of sources); nearest operating airport Aurangabad (~160 km)
travel.railway: Jalgaon Junction (~1-2 km from city localities)
travel.road: Rampeth locality, Jalgaon city; JMTU city buses, autos and taxis available

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter); Ram Navami for the main festival
